display.purpose: Marketing and hero sections only. Never inside the product shell.

headline.purpose: Page-level titles. Maximum one per view.

title.purpose: Section headers, panel headings, card titles.

body.purpose: Default UI text — labels, descriptions, cell content. 14px is the standard product text size.

label.purpose: Metadata, timestamps, compact table headers. 12px is the floor — nothing smaller.

shadows.name: content-hover
shadows.purpose: Cards and list items on hover. Dropdowns, context menus, tooltips. Never at rest.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Default for interactive state changes: border-color, background, box-shadow, color. Short and imperceptible.

motion.name: overlay-enter
motion.purpose: Dropdown, popover, tooltip appear. No bounce.

breakpoints.name: min-width
breakpoints.purpose: Product UI minimum. Desktop-first; no responsive collapse below this.

narrative.overview:
Facelift is an operations layer, not a showpiece. Its interface is built for professional social media managers, community operators, and enterprise marketing teams who are under real pressure and do not have time to decipher a designer's aesthetic statement. The visual system earns trust by being invisible: nothing calls for attention unless it needs to be acted on.

The palette is almost entirely grey and white. Blue enters the frame only to direct action. The dark carbon shell gives the product a grounded, production-grade presence. Content lives on white surfaces. The workspace behind them is light grey. The shell is near-black. Nothing crosses those registers without reason.

The design guidelines are explicit: 'The main interface consists of grey/black/white tones. Blue is the primary color and is used to guide the user to the main action. Do not use decorative elements, shadows or gradients.'
keyCharacteristics: Near-monochromatic interface: shell ink, workspace grey, surface white, one action blue
Reduction as a design principle: space over lines, no decorative elements
Flat at rest; elevation only in response to state (hover, overlay, focus)
One primary blue for direction, status colors for system feedback only
AI features marked with a deliberate violet departure (Lifty Violet)
Dense information capability: 14px body, compact spacing scale, multi-panel layouts
1,140 components — always use the system before writing custom markup

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Directive Blue (#1339ec) is the only color permitted on a primary interactive element. Everything blue is actionable.

rules.name: The Secondary Palette Belongs to Users
rules.body: Extended ramps (cobalt, amber, coral, etc.) are reserved for user-generated content only. The product UI uses grey/white/blue.

rules.name: The Two-Scale Rule
rules.body: In-app UI uses only the BB Update scale (Helvetica Neue). Lota Grotesque never enters the product shell.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: A resting surface has no shadow. Shadows are earned by hover, overlay, or genuine z-elevation.

rules.name: The Filled Chip Rule
rules.body: The active state in navigation is always a filled chip (blue bg + white text for main nav, light grey pill for settings). Never underline, left border, or bold text alone.

rules.name: The Diamond Rule
rules.body: Post status on calendar cards uses a ◆ diamond icon + label, never a pill chip. Pill chips are reserved for sentiment badges only.

rules.name: The White Sidebar Rule
rules.body: The expanded sidebar is always Surface Base white. Only the icon-only collapsed sidebar uses Shell Ink.

dos: Do use Directive Blue (#1339ec) on one CTA per screen.
Do place content surfaces on white lifted from Studio Grey. Maintain the three-tier depth structure.
Do use a filled chip (blue bg + white text) as the active indicator in main navigation.
Do show item counts as plain secondary text. Never wrap counts in badge chips.
Do use ◆ diamond + label for post status on calendar cards. Pill chips are for sentiment only.
Do show tag chips as first two + grey +N overflow. Never wrap to a second row.
Do keep the expanded sidebar white. Only the collapsed icon sidebar is Shell Ink.
Do mark every AI feature with Lifty Violet and the Facelift AI icon.
Do apply shadows on hover or overlaid layers only. Never on resting cards.
Do use aria-label on every icon-only button.
Do wrap non-essential transitions in @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce).
Do use 2px Directive Blue border for selected calendar cards — background stays white.
donts: Don't use heavy gradients, flashy micro-animations, or visual decoration that performs excitement.
Don't replicate Hootsuite/Buffer: cluttered hierarchies, legacy tables, dense chrome.
Don't add a resting shadow to a card or list item.
Don't use border-left/border-right as a colored accent stripe on cards or callouts. The only sanctioned left border is the selected-state in Engage feed list items.
Don't use blur or glassmorphism effects.
Don't use Lota Grotesque inside the product UI.
Don't use secondary ramps (cobalt, amber, coral, etc.) for product UI elements.
Don't use Lifty Violet outside AI feature contexts.
Don't place more than one primary blue button on a screen.
Don't rely on color alone for status — always pair with text label and/or icon.
Don't stack multiple system banners. One at a time.
Don't hide disabled menu items. Keep them visible with --sys-text-disabled.
Don't use pill chips for post status on calendar cards.
Don't use a background tint for selected cards. Use the 2px blue border.
Don't make the expanded sidebar dark.
